newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jobs come before EMU "decimal points" - Fabius.
newsitem.headline: Jobs come before EMU "decimal points" - Fabius.

text.p: Socialist National Assembly speaker Laurent Fabius said on Tuesday that the French Socialists favoured launching the single European currency on time in 1999 but "employment should not be sacrificed in a fixation with decimal points".

"We are, for our part, in favour of the single currency and the date but, as the prime minister (Lionel Jospin) stated clearly during the election campaign, on four precise conditions, particularly that the euro is at the service of employment, not the reverse," he said.

"We clearly have to manage public finances seriously. But it would be a mistake to sacrifice employment in a fixation with decimal points. We're not fetishists," Fabius told a conference on France-German relations.
He was referring to targets for joining the single currency, which include limiting public deficits to three percent of gross domestic product.

Jospin and his new left-wing coalition say fitness to join the euro launch must be measured in terms of the trend towards three percent. The Maastricht treaty, which lays down rules for economic and monetary union, does not stipulate a strict 3.0 percent goal for public deficits, they say.
"The serious attachment to the Franco-German alliance cannot serve as a substitute for a clear idea on the future of European construction," Fabius said.
